title: standards.json — the external competency spine and its crosswalk

rights.description: Whether this framework's identifiers and unit titles may be reproduced here. Deliberately mirrors the instrument_rights.json posture: a grant is quoted verbatim and captured with a date, never summarised, because a permission sentence on a web page can change without notice.

status.description: granted means an affirmative third-party educational grant was located and quoted. not-established means no grant was found — which is NOT the same as no grant existing, and must not be treated as a refusal.

grantText.description: The permission language VERBATIM. Required when status is granted.

archivedCopy.description: Repo-relative path to a dated capture of the permission page. Required when status is granted — this, not the live URL, is the record of what the source said.

titlesReproducible.description: May this framework's unit TITLES be shown verbatim on a shipped page? False forces reference mode: cite the identifier, paraphrase the title.

rotationRequirement.description: For the 4-week adult inpatient resident rotation only. 'elsewhere' means the program addresses it on a different rotation and this one is correctly silent — that is a coverage ANSWER, not a gap.

internalCodes.description: Mapped internal content codes. An EMPTY array is meaningful and is not a defect on its own — but it is not automatically innocent either. Every unit with an empty array must declare a mappingStatus saying WHICH kind of empty it is; bin/check_standards_coverage.py refuses an unexplained one and reports the three kinds separately.

mappingStatus.description: REQUIRED when internalCodes is empty, and FORBIDDEN when it is not. Why this unit maps to nothing. `answered-elsewhere`: the rotation does not teach it, so silence here is the answer. `blocked-on-vocabulary`: mappable the day a named code is added or split — a REAL content gap, and mappingBlockedBy must name the missing code. `category-mismatch`: genuinely inexpressible in a disorder taxonomy, for all time — deliberately hard to earn and currently unused, so check first whether the unit is really just blocked on a code nobody has written. Added 2026-09-14 because a single report line was calling all ten unmapped units 'not a content gap' while nine of them carried notes reading 'VOCABULARY GAP'.

mappingBlockedBy.description: REQUIRED when mappingStatus is 'blocked-on-vocabulary'. The code that does not exist yet, in words — e.g. 'no psychotherapy code exists in the twelve-code vocabulary'. A gap nobody named is a gap nobody fixes, so the checker will not accept the status without it.

blockedByCode.description: REQUIRED when mappingStatus is 'blocked-on-vocabulary'. The id of the PROPOSED code in vocabulary.json that would unblock this unit. Prose says what is missing; this says which queue entry delivers it, so the payoff of adding a code is computable rather than argued. bin/check_vocabulary.py verifies BOTH directions — the code must exist, must be proposed (not already active), and must list this unit in its own `unblocks`.

review.description: Faculty review of this unit's rotation requirement and mapping. Nothing here is publishable while pending.
